tooltip: Before you begin: You can deduct moving expenses only if you are a Member of the Armed Forces on active duty and, due to a military order, you, your spouse, or your dependents move because of a permanent change of station, or you are a Member of the Intelligence Community who moves due to a change in assignment that requires relocation. Check here to certify that you meet these requirements. See the instructions.
1. Transportation and storage of household goods and personal effects (see instructions).
2. Travel (including lodging) from your old home to your new home (see instructions). Do not include the cost of meals.

4. Enter the total amount the government paid you for the expenses listed on lines 1 and 2 that is not included in box 1 of your Form W-2 (wages). This amount should be shown in box 12 of your Form W-2 with code P.

5. Is line 3 more than line 4? No. You cannot deduct your moving expenses. If line 3 is less than line 4, subtract line 3 from line 4 and include the result on Form 1040, 1040-S R, or 1040-N R, line 1h.
5. Yes. Subtract line 4 from line 3. Enter the result here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 14. This is your moving expense deduction.
